detail: The structural guarantee (§12.2: a derived row must be structurally incapable of being returned to a caller asking for observations) is physical separation by DATASET NAME, not a nullable-id join like the odds adapter used. BitemporalStore.as_of()/observations() glob only the one dataset directory they are asked for, so a derived row never written under an observed dataset's name is physically absent from any query against that name. schemas.register_derived_capability enforces a 'derived_' dataset-name prefix at registration time (both directions: is_modelled=True requires the prefix, and the prefix requires is_modelled=True), checked against the existing static schema table at import time too, not just for new registrations. derived.write_derived stamps is_modelled/derived_from/calibration onto every row itself and rejects a caller DataFrame that already carries any of those columns — a caller cannot control is_modelled's value at all, closing the 'a flag a caller might forget' failure mode explicitly.

The guarantee's honest boundary: BitemporalStore.write() itself (unmodified, not owned by this story) has zero awareness of is_modelled and will accept a forged is_modelled=True/False under any dataset name without complaint — proven directly by tests/test_derived.py::test_store_write_itself_has_no_is_modelled_awareness. The guarantee holds only because write_derived is the sole path this codebase uses to persist a derived row, the same trust relationship every other capability already has with store.write() (Provider.fetch() validates before store.write(), which never re-validates). This is a scope boundary, not a gap: adding is_modelled enforcement inside store.py would be a store-wide design decision (should every write be schema-validated?) that belongs to the Architect, flagged in docs/wiki/provider-framework.md §15.2 rather than silently routed around.

olbauday's observed_at_source/observed_at_imputed columns should NOT fold into is_modelled — they are a different axis. is_modelled means the row's VALUE is computed, not measured; observed_at_imputed means the row's value is a genuine observation but the TIMESTAMP it is dated under is inferred. Conflating them would mix 'we estimated what happened' with 'we estimated when we learned it', different failure modes with different consumers. What generalised instead: the column-pair PATTERN itself, now documented as a reusable convention (schemas.py's DERIVED_PROVENANCE_FIELDS comment) so the next adapter needing an imputed-timestamp pair does not reinvent the column names a third time. Full reasoning in docs/wiki/provider-framework.md §15.3.

detail: vaastav_player_gameweek_stats.expected_goals is verified live 100% NULL for 2019-20/2020-21/2021-22 and 100% populated 2022-23 onward -- a hard per-season boundary, not a gradual thinning. Fit design: every match enters one quasi-Poisson MLE for attack/defence/home-advantage, target = team xG where available else team goals, goals-sourced matches down-weighted (goals_source_weight, default 0.6, UNCALIBRATED placeholder) relative to xG-sourced ones.
